label: exr:i01-01
hint: Use distributivity on \(a(v+(-v))\) and identify the additive inverse of \(av\).

label: exr:i01-03
hint: Use pointwise addition and scalar multiplication, then check that continuity is preserved by both operations.

label: exr:i01-04
hint: Check whether the zero vector belongs to the set; scalar closure gives a second quick test.

label: exr:i01-05
hint: Ask which scalars are available. Over \(\mathbb C\), \(1\) suffices; over \(\mathbb R\), separate real and imaginary parts.

label: exr:i01-07
hint: Check the vector-space axioms entrywise; identify the zero matrix and additive inverses.

label: exr:i01-08
hint: Use associativity repeatedly; a short induction on the number of summands formalizes the argument.

label: exr:i03-02
hint: Solve \(a(1,0)+b(1,1)=(3,2)\) directly; the coefficients you obtain are the coordinates.

label: exr:i03-05
hint: A basis of \(U\) is an independent list in \(V\) with \(\dim V\) vectors; use the dimension bound for independent lists.

label: exr:i04-06
hint: Track only how the coordinate entries are reordered, and test the rule on basis coordinate vectors.

label: exr:i04-07
hint: Keep the abstract vector fixed and compare only its coordinate columns in two different bases.

label: exr:i04-08
hint: Use the explicit inverse for a nearly parallel basis and observe the entries of size \(1/\varepsilon\).

label: exr:i05-02
hint: Test the zero vector first: a linear map must send \(0\) to \(0\).

label: exr:i05-05
hint: Write an arbitrary vector as a linear combination of the basis and use linearity of both maps.

label: exr:i05-06
hint: Try a coordinate shift such as \(N(x,y)=(y,0)\) and compute \(N^2\).

label: exr:i05-07
hint: Define addition and scalar multiplication pointwise on maps and verify the vector-space axioms.

label: exr:i06-01
hint: Set \(T(x,y,z)=0\) and solve the resulting homogeneous equations.

label: exr:i06-02
hint: Use rank--nullity after computing the kernel dimension in the preceding exercise.

label: exr:i06-03
hint: If \(T(v)=T(w)\), apply linearity to \(v-w\); for the converse compare \(T(v)\) with \(T(0)\).

label: exr:i06-04
hint: Surjectivity means \(\operatorname{im}T=W\); compare the dimensions of these spaces.

label: exr:i06-05
hint: Extend a basis of \(U\) to a basis of \(V\) and inspect the cosets of the added basis vectors.

label: exr:i07-02
hint: The coordinate vector of the \(j\)-th domain basis vector is \(e_j\); multiplying by the matrix selects column \(j\).

label: exr:i07-04
hint: Identify one nonzero column and show that every other column is a scalar multiple of it.

label: exr:i07-06
hint: Apply the reflection to \(e_1\) and \(e_2\); those two images are the matrix columns.

label: exr:i07-07
hint: Use explicit transformations whose compositions depend on order, such as a projection and a rotation.

label: exr:i08-04
hint: For a diagonal matrix, only the identity permutation contributes to the determinant.

label: exr:i08-05
hint: Use cyclicity \(\operatorname{tr}(XY)=\operatorname{tr}(YX)\) with a factorization that places \(P^{-1}P\) together.

label: exr:i08-06
hint: Choose a basis consisting of one normal direction and a basis of the reflecting hyperplane, then read the diagonal matrix.

label: exr:i08-07
hint: Write the diagonal entries of \(uv^T\) explicitly and add them.

label: exr:i08-08
hint: Two matrices of the same endomorphism in different bases are similar; use multiplicativity of determinant and cyclicity of trace.

label: exr:i09-03
hint: If the zero vector were allowed, it would satisfy \(T0=\lambda0\) for every scalar \(\lambda\); explain why that carries no spectral information.

label: exr:i09-04
hint: Use \(E_\lambda=\ker(T-\lambda I)\) and the fact that kernels of linear maps are subspaces.

label: exr:i09-05
hint: Compare the roots of the same characteristic polynomial over \(\mathbb R\) and over \(\mathbb C\).

label: exr:i10-01
hint: If \(v\in E_\lambda\), compute \(T(v)\) and check that it remains in the same eigenspace.

label: exr:i10-04
hint: For a diagonal operator, try the span of any subset of eigenbasis vectors.

label: exr:i10-05
hint: A real triangular matrix has real diagonal eigenvalues; compare this with a real rotation having no real eigenvalue.

label: exr:i10-06
hint: The matrix \(tI-A\) is triangular; take the product of its diagonal entries.

label: exr:i11-04
hint: Use \(V=\operatorname{im}P\oplus\ker P\) and determine how \(P\) acts on each summand.

label: exr:i11-07
hint: Use the Lagrange polynomial that is \(1\) at \(\lambda_i\) and \(0\) at every other eigenvalue.

label: exr:i13-03
hint: A vector \((a,b)\) is orthogonal to every vector on the \(x\)-axis exactly when its first coordinate is zero.

label: exr:i13-04
hint: Expand both squared norms and cancel the cross terms.

label: exr:i13-06
hint: If \(v\in U\cap U^\perp\), test \(\langle v,v\rangle\).

label: exr:i14-05
hint: In reduced QR with full column rank, \(Q\) has one orthonormal column for each column of \(A\), while \(R\) is square \(n\times n\).

label: exr:i15-02
hint: Take determinants in \(Q^TQ=I\) and use \(\det(Q^T)=\det Q\).

label: exr:i15-03
hint: Set \(P=uu^T\); use \(P^2=P=P^T\) to compute \((I-2P)^T(I-2P)\).

label: exr:i15-04
hint: Apply the unitary operator to an orthonormal basis and use inner-product preservation.

label: exr:i15-05
hint: Use \(Q^{-1}=Q^*\), then compute the adjoint of \(Q^{-1}\).

label: exr:i15-06
hint: A diagonal matrix with one \(-1\) and the remaining diagonal entries \(1\) gives an immediate example.

label: exr:i15-07
hint: If \(Uv=\lambda v\), compare \(\|Uv\|\) with \(\|v\|\).

label: exr:i16-01
hint: For \(Tv=\lambda v\), compare \(\langle Tv,v\rangle\) with \(\langle v,Tv\rangle\) using the stated complex convention.

label: exr:i16-02
hint: Find the two eigenspaces, normalize one vector in each, and use them as columns of an orthogonal matrix.

label: exr:i16-03
hint: Use \(U^*U=UU^*=I\).

label: exr:i16-04
hint: Apply positivity to an eigenvector: \(\langle Tv,v\rangle=\lambda\|v\|^2\).

label: exr:i16-06
hint: For \(w\in U^\perp\) and \(u\in U\), rewrite \(\langle Tw,u\rangle\) using self-adjointness.

label: exr:i17-02
hint: Expand \(q(u+v)\) using bilinearity and symmetry, then solve for \(B(u,v)\).

label: exr:i17-03
hint: Substitute \(x=Py\) into \(x^TAx\) and collect the two factors of \(P\).

label: exr:i17-06
hint: If \(Av=0\) for a nonzero vector \(v\), evaluate \(v^TAv\).

label: exr:i17-07
hint: Use the orthogonal variables \(u=(x+y)/\sqrt2\), \(v=(x-y)/\sqrt2\), then solve for \(x,y\).

label: exr:i18-01
hint: Compute \(A^*A\); the singular values are the nonnegative square roots of its eigenvalues.

label: exr:i18-02
hint: For any \(v\), compute \(\langle A^*Av,v\rangle=\|Av\|^2\).

label: exr:i18-03
hint: One inclusion is immediate; for the converse use \(\langle A^*Av,v\rangle=\|Av\|^2\).

label: exr:i18-05
hint: Reciprocate only the positive diagonal singular values and transpose the rectangular shape.

label: exr:i18-06
hint: Diagonalization requires an endomorphism; SVD instead uses orthonormal bases in the domain and codomain separately.
